Engage Plays

Account Activation Request

From Inactive to Active — Contact, FEIN, AP Contact & Billing  •  Sales Team Quick Guide  •  Accounts Module

Why This Play Matters

New accounts start as Inactive / No Sell — nothing can be quoted or sold until the record is complete. This flow walks you through the setup that matters: the contact, the FEIN from the W-9, the AP Contact, billing, and surcharges. Once everything is saved, the account becomes active — notify your Sales Manager to approve it for sale.

The Play at a Glance

1. Add the Contact
2. Enter the FEIN
3. Set the AP Contact
4. Bill To & Surcharges
5. Save, Go Active & Get Approval
1
Add the Contact

Go to Contacts in the left navigation and create the new contact. Complete the following before moving on:

  • First Name / Last Name — both are required fields (marked with a red asterisk).
  • Account — tie the contact to the correct account under the Company section. This link is what makes the contact selectable as the AP Contact in Step 3.
  • Title & Job Functions — for an AP Contact, tag the Accounts Payable job function so billing knows who to reach.
  • Phone & Email — add at least one of each. Invoices and credit communications route to this contact.

Click Save in the top-right before leaving the page.

2
Enter the FEIN from the W-9

Open the account record. On the General tab, select the Basic Information sub-tab.

  • Request a W-9 from the client and any standard onboarding documents they have.
  • Tax ID/EIN — enter the FEIN exactly as it is stated on the customer's W-9. No guessing, no pulling from a website — the W-9 is the source of truth.
  • While you're here: confirm the Account Name, Industry, and Company Address match the W-9 and customer records.
3
Set the AP Contact on the Account

Move to the A/R Status sub-tab. Notice the account still shows Inactive and No Sell in the top-right — that's expected until this setup is complete and activation is requested.

  • Click the AP Contact dropdown. Every contact tied to the account appears with their phone and email — pick the contact you created in Step 1.
  • Don't see them? Use Create New directly in the dropdown or go back to Step 1 and confirm that the contact is linked to this account.
4
Confirm Bill To & Update Surcharges

Still on the A/R Status sub-tab, finish the billing setup:

  • Default Bill To — confirm whether this customer bills to the Master Account or to individual Sites. Get this from the customer — it drives where every invoice goes.
  • Bill To Same as Company Address — toggle on when billing goes to the address in Basic Information.
  • Surcharges — toggle on any that apply (Service Charge, Credit Card Surcharge) and select the matching Add-On Types: Ship/Hand-In, Ship/Hand-Out, Restock Fee, DO Tax Due, Fuel Surcharge, CC Surcharge, or Not Applicable.
  • Payment Terms & Methods — confirm Net Terms, Hold Period, and Electric/Lighting Payment Methods match how this customer will buy.
5
Save, Go Active & Request Approval to Sell
  • Click Save in the top-right. Unsaved changes do not count — the account will not update until you save.
  • Confirm the account shows Active. With the contact, FEIN, AP Contact, and billing setup complete and saved, the status badge moves to Active — but the account still shows No Sell.
  • Post a note tagging your Sales Manager. In the Notes panel, tag @Sales Manager and request review: "Please review this account and confirm it's approved to sell." This is what starts the approval to sell.
  • Verify before you promise. The account is not ready to transact until your Sales Manager approves and the No Sell flag clears. Confirm both before telling the customer we're ready to go.

Common Misses — Check Before You Walk Away

  • Contact created but not linked to the account — it won't appear in the AP Contact dropdown.
  • FEIN typed from memory instead of the W-9 — it must match the W-9 exactly.
  • Default Bill To left on the wrong setting — Master vs. Sites changes where every invoice lands.
  • Applicable surcharges left off — they can't be added to the invoice after the fact without friction.
  • Everything filled in but Save never clicked — the account can't go Active without a saved record.
  • Account is Active, but no note posted — your Sales Manager can't approve a request they never got.
